name: HandoutFormatter
description:
**Handout Formatter** takes the plain text you've already written in a handout's Notes or GM Notes and dresses it up to look like a real prop from your game world — an old letter, a wanted poster, a torn journal page, whatever fits the scene. You can also use it the other way around: pick one look and apply it across every handout in your game, so everything matches your game system's theme instead of looking like plain, unstyled text. Your original writing is never lost or overwritten — the styling sits on top of it, and can be swapped or removed again at any time.

**A few things people use it for:**

- A handwritten letter or diary page for a journal-keeping character
- A wanted poster, tavern notice, or other in-world prop
- Giving every handout in a game — not just one — the same consistent, system-appropriate look

**Quick start:**

1. Type `!formathandout` in chat to open the control panel.
2. Click a handout in the list to select it (Recent, the A-Z strip, or Search help with a long list).
3. Choose Notes or GM Notes with the toggle in the header.
4. Pick a style under "Preview Style" and check the live preview.
5. Click Apply. Remove Styling, or applying a different style, can always change or undo it later.

**Styles are just handouts.** Every style is a plain CSS handout named `<Name>_css` — open it like any other handout to read or edit its CSS directly, no special editor needed. Four styles (Parchment, 5e, Book, Computer) ship built in; a growing library of additional ready-made styles (Monument, Notebook, Letter, Newspaper, Wanted, Dossier, Chalkboard, Journal, Scroll, PF2) is available in this repo's [style-library.md](https://github.com/keithcurtis1/roll20-api-scripts/blob/master/HandoutFormatter/style-library.md) — just paste one's CSS into a handout named to match and it shows up in the picker automatically. Writing your own style is plain CSS; no scripting required.

**Keeping styled content in sync:** if a styled handout's Notes/GM Notes gets hand-edited afterward, the panel's "Unsynced" filter finds every handout in that state, and "Sync All" re-applies each one's bound style in a single click.

**Works well with:** [Image Editor](https://app.roll20.net/forum/post/12716858/script-image-editor-format-images-add-captions-and-flow-text-in-roll20-handouts), a separate script for placing and captioning images inside a handout — if it's installed, a button in the panel jumps straight to it.

Everything beyond the two commands below is click-driven from inside the control panel:

- `!formathandout` — opens the control panel
- `!formathandout --help` — opens the in-game help handout
